A1.justification: Both PDFs contain complete, readable versions of the same HeteroRL/GEPO study. All 35 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison after matching the reorganized supplementary material.

before.justification: v8 reports original Qwen3 mathematical-reasoning experiments, latency and hyperparameter studies, ablations and empirical bias measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v9 retains these original experiments and measurements, including the benchmark results in Tables 1–4 and the reorganized supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The described HeteroRL architecture, GEPO group-expectation weighting, objectives, Listing 1 and localized reward computation are unchanged. Defensive sampling remains a proposed future direction rather than a newly implemented component.

E1.justification: Both versions retain MATH levels 3–5 training and evaluation on AMC2023, AIME2024, AIME2025 and MATH500. Online, heterogeneous-delay, think/non-think and network-latency scenarios remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain GRPO, GSPO, BNPO and Dr.GRPO. The asynchronous comparison retains Truncated IS+KL, TOPR with/without KL and CISPO with/without KL, moving from v8 Table 9 to v9 Table 12. New on-policy/off-policy headings only categorize existing comparators.

E3.justification: The 8,290 training samples, Pass@1 evaluation over eight sampled responses, model sizes, 2k/4k output limits, training budgets, delay settings and KL controls are retained. The relocated hyperparameter studies use the same settings and sweeps.

E4.justification: The documented importance-weight and advantage-normalization ablations, latency tests, hyperparameter sensitivities, think/non-think analysis, empirical bias study and case study are retained. Their relocation introduces no new diagnostic analysis or removes any detailed study.

E5.justification: The correlation analysis retains its 95% confidence intervals and significance threshold. The 512-step Monte Carlo bias summaries and other appendix statistics are unchanged; no repeated-run, seed or uncertainty-reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: All matched quantitative results and plotted findings are unchanged, including GEPO's 62.6 best and 60.8 last averages in Table 2. However, v9 deletes the unquantified statement on v8 page 12 that defensive-sampling experiments enhanced training stability, removing a limited qualitative finding.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–3, Lemma 1, Corollary 1, formal assumptions and derivations are retained. Moving v8 Appendix J into v9 A.2 renumbers equations without changing their mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same HeteroRL framework contribution, latency/KL instability argument and GEPO variance-reduction and stability claims. The headline 3% latency-related drop and 85% best-to-last-gap reduction claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations of latency-induced instability, bias–variance tradeoffs, think/non-think behavior and correlation versus causation are retained, as are qualifications about residual high-delay instability. Defensive-sampling motivation remains unchanged in v8 G.1 and v9 H.1.

D1.justification: The implementation disclosures retain the same hyperparameters, three-epoch budget, vLLM/FSDP probability recomputation, ZeroMQ communication logic and code-access link. Moving implementation and sensitivity details does not add or revise operational instructions.

R1.justification: The reference list and Section 5 are unchanged. However, v9 removes the page-12 assertion that no existing literature had documented or proposed defensive sampling, withdrawing a narrow novelty claim about that future direction.

P1.justification: The appendix hierarchy is substantially reorganized: v8 A/J become v9 A, L becomes B.5, and K becomes C.1, with corresponding contents and cross-reference updates. Smaller edits add baseline-category headings, correct the duplicated Figure 8b reference and update authorship/funding text. The new hierarchy leaves two headings numbered A.1.

P2.justification: The appendix layout extensively relocates existing displays: bias Figure 13 becomes Figure 9, hyperparameter Tables 10–15 become Tables 5–10, and the asynchronous comparison moves to Table 12/Figure 12. Pagination and surrounding text reflow substantially. Figure 1 also receives limited equation and label typesetting changes; the displayed data are retained.

improvement.justification: Consolidating the previously separated theory and sensitivity studies in Appendices A and B makes the supporting material easier to follow. This is a limited organizational improvement; the method, proofs and detailed experimental evidence remain unchanged. Small drawbacks include duplicate A.1 numbering and loss of the defensive-sampling model attribution when its unquantified success and novelty paragraph is deleted.
